summary_en: This single-arm Phase 2 study tests an internal radiation boost called high-dose-rate rectal brachytherapy, using Iridium-192, in people with low-lying residual rectal adenocarcinoma after total neoadjuvant therapy. The boost is given through an intracavitary applicator in three weekly outpatient fractions, for a total dose of 21 Gy. The study measures whether the treatment is safe and whether it improves organ preservation, meaning patients avoid surgical resection.
summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 de un solo grupo evalúa un refuerzo de radiación interna llamado braquiterapia rectal de alta tasa de dosis, con Iridio-192, en personas con adenocarcinoma rectal residual de localización baja después de la terapia neoadyuvante total. El refuerzo se administra mediante un aplicador intracavitario en tres fracciones semanales ambulatorias, para una dosis total de 21 Gy. El estudio mide si el tratamiento es seguro y si mejora la preservación del órgano, es decir, si los pacientes evitan la resección quirúrgica.
who_for: Adults aged 18 to 100 with MMR-proficient low or mid rectal adenocarcinoma, cT1-4 N0-2 M0.
Incomplete or near-complete response after total neoadjuvant therapy, with surgery expected to be APR or low LAR.
Residual tumor under 4 cm long and 1.2 cm thick, under 50% circumference, above the dentate line.
Restaging 4 to 16 weeks after total neoadjuvant therapy; ECOG 0 to 3.
Platelets above 50, hemoglobin above 8 g/dL, and neutrophil count above 500 meet the stated thresholds.
not_for: History of ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease.
Pelvic radiation given before the rectal cancer external beam radiation.
Prior colorectal surgery with an anastomosis at or near the brachytherapy target.
Uncontrolled severe illness, or life expectancy under 3 years per provider.
Concurrent cytotoxic chemotherapy, immunotherapy, or targeted cancer drugs; pregnancy.
